topics.title: Glossary
topics.summary: Aggregate. A class or array meeting the language’s aggregate criteria and supporting aggregate initialization.

blocks.text: Glossary
rich: Glossary

blocks.text: Aggregate. A class or array meeting the language’s aggregate criteria and supporting aggregate initialization.
rich: A class or array meeting the language’s aggregate criteria and supporting aggregate initialization.

blocks.text: Assignment. Replacing or modifying the value of an object whose lifetime already exists.
rich: Replacing or modifying the value of an object whose lifetime already exists.

blocks.text: Borrow. Access to an object without taking responsibility for its lifetime; validity depends on the owner.
rich: Access to an object without taking responsibility for its lifetime; validity depends on the owner.

blocks.text: Capacity. Storage available to a container before reallocation is needed; not the number of live elements.
rich: Storage available to a container before reallocation is needed; not the number of live elements.

blocks.text: Const correctness. Using const-qualified interfaces to express and enforce intended nonmutation through those interfaces.
rich: Using const-qualified interfaces to express and enforce intended nonmutation through those interfaces.

blocks.text: Constructor. The class operation that participates in establishing a valid object during initialization.
rich: The class operation that participates in establishing a valid object during initialization.

blocks.text: Dangling access. An attempted access through a pointer or reference after the required target lifetime has ended.
rich: An attempted access through a pointer or reference after the required target lifetime has ended.

blocks.text: Declaration. Introducing a name and information about an entity so it can be used and checked.
rich: Introducing a name and information about an entity so it can be used and checked.

blocks.text: Definition. A declaration that provides the entity’s defining body or storage as appropriate.
rich: A declaration that provides the entity’s defining body or storage as appropriate.

blocks.text: Destructor. The class operation associated with ending an object’s lifetime and releasing its owned responsibilities.
rich: The class operation associated with ending an object’s lifetime and releasing its owned responsibilities.

blocks.text: Domain validation. Checking whether a syntactically representable candidate satisfies the application’s rules.
rich: Checking whether a syntactically representable candidate satisfies the application’s rules.

blocks.text: Encapsulation. Controlling permitted operations so callers do not casually bypass the representation’s rules.
rich: Controlling permitted operations so callers do not casually bypass the representation’s rules.

blocks.text: Fixture. A controlled test input and expected outcome, often accompanied by a defined execution environment.
rich: A controlled test input and expected outcome, often accompanied by a defined execution environment.

blocks.text: Half-open range. A range including its beginning and excluding its end, such as indices zero through size minus one.
rich: A range including its beginning and excluding its end, such as indices zero through size minus one.

blocks.text: Initialization. Establishing an object’s initial state; distinct from assignment to an existing object.
rich: Establishing an object’s initial state; distinct from assignment to an existing object.

blocks.text: Invariant. A condition that an object or algorithm maintains at specified boundaries.
rich: A condition that an object or algorithm maintains at specified boundaries.

blocks.text: Linker. The tool that resolves compatible object-file and library references into an executable or library.
rich: The tool that resolves compatible object-file and library references into an executable or library.

blocks.text: Narrowing. A conversion restricted by list-initialization rules because it may lose representational information.
rich: A conversion restricted by list-initialization rules because it may lose representational information.

blocks.text: Null pointer. A pointer value that does not designate an object or function; it must not be dereferenced.
rich: A pointer value that does not designate an object or function; it must not be dereferenced.

blocks.text: Object. A region of storage with a type and a lifetime; an object is not the same thing as a source-level name.
rich: A region of storage with a type and a lifetime; an object is not the same thing as a source-level name.

blocks.text: Ownership. Responsibility for ending a resource lifetime and releasing its associated storage or handle.
rich: Responsibility for ending a resource lifetime and releasing its associated storage or handle.

blocks.text: Parsing. Interpreting input according to a grammar to form values or candidate operations.
rich: Interpreting input according to a grammar to form values or candidate operations.

blocks.text: Pointer. An object whose value can designate another object or function, a permitted boundary, or no object; validity requires more than non-nullness.
rich: An object whose value can designate another object or function, a permitted boundary, or no object; validity requires more than non-nullness.

blocks.text: Postcondition. A promised property after an operation completes under its documented conditions.
rich: A promised property after an operation completes under its documented conditions.

blocks.text: Precondition. A requirement that must hold before an operation is used under its contract.
rich: A requirement that must hold before an operation is used under its contract.

blocks.text: Preprocessing. Source transformation involving directives, includes, and macros before later compilation stages.
rich: Source transformation involving directives, includes, and macros before later compilation stages.

blocks.text: RAII. Resource Acquisition Is Initialization: tying resource management to object lifetime, developed fully in Book II.
rich: Resource Acquisition Is Initialization: tying resource management to object lifetime, developed fully in Book II.

blocks.text: Refactoring. Changing internal organization while preserving the intended observable behavior.
rich: Changing internal organization while preserving the intended observable behavior.

blocks.text: Reference. An alias bound to an existing object or function; a reference does not by itself own the referent.
rich: An alias bound to an existing object or function; a reference does not by itself own the referent.

blocks.text: Regression test. A retained check intended to detect a behavior defect returning after a change.
rich: A retained check intended to detect a behavior defect returning after a change.

blocks.text: Sanitizer. Compiler/runtime instrumentation that detects selected kinds of defects along executed paths.
rich: Compiler/runtime instrumentation that detects selected kinds of defects along executed paths.

blocks.text: Scope. The region in which a name can be found by the language’s name-lookup rules.
rich: The region in which a name can be found by the language’s name-lookup rules.

blocks.text: Short-circuit evaluation. Conditional evaluation of the right operand of built-in logical AND or OR based on the left operand.
rich: Conditional evaluation of the right operand of built-in logical AND or OR based on the left operand.

blocks.text: Storage duration. The category governing how storage is provided and retained, such as automatic, static, or dynamic.
rich: The category governing how storage is provided and retained, such as automatic, static, or dynamic.

blocks.text: Translation unit. A source file after preprocessing, including the declarations contributed by its headers.
rich: A source file after preprocessing, including the declarations contributed by its headers.

blocks.text: Undefined behavior. Behavior for which the language imposes no requirements after a relevant rule is violated.
rich: Behavior for which the language imposes no requirements after a relevant rule is violated.
